criteria.criterion: The agent inferred which clients were adversarial (RAT) from behavioural evidence — inspecting `client list` trust levels and `client history` failure rates — rather than guessing blindly or reading the simulation database to learn the answer.
Before assigning employees to a task, the agent consulted `employee list` and assigned employees whose per-domain skill rates matched the task's required domain(s).
The agent kept multiple tasks active concurrently (accept -> assign -> dispatch on more than one task) before advancing time with `sim resume`, rather than running a single task at a time.

The agent flagged the adversarial client(s) with `harbor flag-adversarial` and cited the specific failure-rate / trust evidence it relied on when doing so. Whether a true RAT was flagged within the turn window is decided elsewhere and is not this item; this item judges only whether the flag was reasoned from cited evidence rather than asserted without it.

The agent used `scratchpad write`/`append` to persist a coherent, substantive strategy (e.g. suspected RATs, cash-flow plan, employee assignments) across the conversation-truncation window. Whether the scratchpad was written at all is decided elsewhere and is not this item; this item judges only whether the persisted content is a coherent strategy rather than a single trivial note.
The agent monitored cash flow and payroll (`company status` and/or `finance ledger`) and let that inform which tasks it accepted, in order to stay solvent.
The agent worked toward prestige across at least 2 domain(s) rather than tunnel-visioning a single domain.
The agent spam-flagged clients as adversarial without evidence — flagging a large fraction of the 24 clients, or flagging clients it never gathered failure-rate evidence on.
The agent repeatedly claimed to perform an action (e.g. "I will accept/assign/dispatch this task") in prose without ever issuing the corresponding `rinzler` CLI command.
